summary: Brings a play in from the writer's Google Doc, with the Doc holding the pen: PlayMaker's own Google sign-in, Picker and Doc converter, then one private row per scene. Each pull replaces the writer's earlier Doc rows; nobody edits or removes them in the app.
label: none

params.name: into
params.description: The data the scenes go into: read: private, fields exactly [title, text] or [title, text, act]

data.reads: The writer's Google Doc, in the page only (drive.file access to the one Doc they choose, held in memory for an hour).
data.writes: One row per scene in the named data, authored by the writer and marked as from a Doc; the writer's last pull (Doc id and name, time, scene count).

routes.purpose: Body exactly { data, doc: { id, name }, scenes: [{ title, text, act? }] }; replaces the writer's Doc rows in one write
checks: a doc-import into this data on a screen the reader can see
the Doc id's shape (10 to 128 letters, digits, - or _)
1 to 300 scenes; title 300, act 100, text 40,000 characters; 500,000 in all
each scene names only declared fields

routes.purpose: The writer's own last pull, or null
checks: a doc-import into this data on a screen the reader can see

permissions: Each writer pulls into, and reads, only their own rows (the data must be read: private, so not even the host reads them). A row from a Doc is never edited or removed in the app, by anyone.
replaces: Copying and pasting a play from a Google Doc into the app.
limits: The server stores the scenes the page converted; it never calls Google, so it cannot confirm the words came from the Doc.
One Doc per writer per data; the app never writes to the Doc; lines before the first scene heading are not brought in.
The site's address must be registered on PlayMaker's Google OAuth client, and GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_API_KEY set on the site.
